description: Short, self-contained research-note questions for the NOUS chat workflow.

cases.question: Use only this note: 'Researchers tested a search tool with 20 students. Students found papers faster with the tool.' Summarize it in one sentence.
cases.referenceAnswer: Researchers tested a search tool with 20 students, who found papers faster with it.

cases.question: Use only this note: 'A study compared keyword search and semantic search. Semantic search found more relevant papers.' What was the main finding?
cases.referenceAnswer: Semantic search found more relevant papers than keyword search.

cases.question: Use only this note: 'Researchers interviewed 12 librarians about how they choose papers.' How was the study done?
cases.referenceAnswer: Researchers interviewed 12 librarians about how they choose papers.

cases.question: Use only this note: 'The tool was tested with five students at one university.' What is one limitation?
cases.referenceAnswer: The sample was small: only five students took part.

cases.question: Which note supports the claim that summaries saved reading time? Note A: 'Summaries reduced reading time.' Note B: 'Search found more papers.'
cases.referenceAnswer: Note A supports that claim because it says summaries reduced reading time.

cases.question: Use only these notes. Paper A: 'The tool saved reading time.' Paper B: 'The tool did not save reading time.' Compare them in one sentence.
cases.referenceAnswer: Paper A found that the tool saved reading time, while Paper B found that it did not.

cases.question: Use only this note: 'Researchers compared two search methods. Results are not included.' Can you identify which method worked better? Briefly explain your answer.
cases.referenceAnswer: The note does not say which method worked better because the results are missing.

cases.question: My paper note says only 'Deep learning survey, 2021.' In a short reply, how should I verify this citation and handle missing details without guessing?
cases.referenceAnswer: Mark the citation incomplete, find the original source, and do not invent authors, a journal, DOI, or publication status.

requiredConcepts: check the original note or source
verify the record against a reliable source
verify the citation against a reliable source
verify the bibliographic details against a reliable source

forbiddenPatterns.reason: unverified publication status in the proposed citation

cases.question: Use only this note: 'Paper A tested a search tool with ten students. It found more relevant papers. The sample was small.' Draft a short research note here in chat with the finding and limitation.
cases.referenceAnswer: Paper A found more relevant papers with its search tool, but its sample of ten students was small.

requiredConcepts: sample of ten students was small

cases.question: Use only this note: 'A search tool worked well in one small study. It has not been tested with a larger group.' What follow-up study should researchers do to address the stated evidence gap?
cases.referenceAnswer: Researchers should test whether the tool works well with a larger group.

requiredConcepts: bigger and more diverse participant group
forbiddenPhrases: already tested with a larger group

cases.question: Paper note: 'The tool was tested only with librarians. No students took part.' What evidence is missing before recommending it to students?
cases.referenceAnswer: Evidence from testing the tool with students.

cases.question: Paper note: 'Everyone used the new search tool. Nobody used the old tool.' What comparison is missing?
cases.referenceAnswer: A comparison with the old tool.
